summary: Iter 30: Tested new chat extensions — mute toggle, @mentions, attachments (image/PDF base64), web-push subscribe/unsubscribe, push/config, history cap CHAT_HISTORY_MAX=10. Backend: 10/10 new tests pass + iter29 12/12 regression still green (22/22 total in 7s). Frontend desktop UI: mute toggle works (toast + title flip), mention autocomplete menu opens on typing '@', attachment paperclip opens picker, preview shown with clear X, image renders inline after send; push button click is wired correctly (the headless browser shows 'Permission denied' toast as expected). Found ONE real UX bug: mention insertion doubles the '@' character because insertMention() does not strip the user-typed trigger '@' before inserting '@<Name> ', producing '@@Lakshmi Iyer '. Backend still detects the mention thanks to regex tolerance, but visually wrong.

ui_bugs.issue: When the mention autocomplete is triggered by typing '@', clicking the suggestion inserts '@<Name> ' at the cursor without removing the trigger '@' the user already typed. Result: '@@Lakshmi Iyer '. Backend regex @<First> still matches (offset by 1), so the mention is detected and counted, but the rendered message bubble shows '@@Lakshmi Iyer' and the chat-mention highlight span only wraps the substring starting at the inner '@'. Fix: in insertMention(), scan back from cursor for the trigger '@' and replace from that position; or strip the most recent '@' before inserting.

action_items: Fix ChatPage.jsx insertMention(): replace the user-typed '@' trigger character with '@<Name> ' instead of appending after it. Suggested: walk back from cursor to find the latest '@' (until whitespace), then slice that out before injecting insertText.
(Optional/nice-to-have, not blocking) When ChatHeader peer name is not present in a queryable element, expose peer.name on the chat-window root via data-attribute for easier test targeting.
critical_code_review_comments: messaging.py send_message: contains a duplicate `return out_msg` statement (line 609-610). Dead code — second return is unreachable but harmless. Worth cleaning up.

messaging.py _detect_mentions allows '@<First Last>' or '@<First>' to match the peer; double '@' (`@@Name`) is still tolerated because the regex anchors on '@' (non-greedy). Document this lenient behavior — it accidentally rescues the insertMention UX bug above.
messaging.py _trim_conversation_history: deletes with $lte cutoff (cutoff = (cap+1)th newest). This keeps exactly cap rows. Verified by test: after 15 sends, GET returns ≤ 10.

messaging.py push_subscribe: upserts by endpoint only (no per-user scope) — fine because endpoints are globally unique per browser/install. But unsubscribe filters by endpoint AND user_id which is correctly defensive.
messaging.py _vapid_private_pem: silently returns None on bad base64 — webpush then no-ops, masking misconfiguration. Consider logging a warning so ops can see VAPID is broken.
messaging.py send_message: when peer is muted AND no mention, push is correctly skipped. When mention is present and peer is offline, push is sent regardless of mute. ✓ matches spec.

Frontend useWebPush.js (not viewed inline but called from chat-enable-push-btn): caught console toast 'Permission denied' — works as designed in headless. In a real browser the prompt would appear; recommend exposing a fallback hint when Notification.permission === 'denied' so users know to flip the browser setting.

Frontend ChatPage MessageBubble renderText: chat-mention class is only added when the regex matches against `peer.name` (case-insensitive). With the @@ double-prefix bug, the visual highlight starts at the inner @, so the leading lone @ stays unstyled. Both backend mention detection and unread counter still increment correctly.

success_rate.frontend: Desktop ~95% (mute, mentions menu, attachment, push wiring all OK; one UX bug on @@ doubling)

After main agent fixes the @@ doubling in insertMention(), re-test by: (1) login as priya, (2) open chat to a parent, (3) page.keyboard.type('@'), (4) click [data-testid=chat-mention-suggest], (5) read [data-testid=chat-input].value — expected '@<Name> ' (single @). For the mobile layout bug from iter29, this iter's mute/mention controls live inside chat-window header so the bug may still hide the controls on mobile; was not retested here because main agent's mobile CSS fix wasn't in scope of this iteration.
rca of the issue: @@ doubling RCA — ChatPage.jsx line 440 `insertMention` does string-splice insert of '@<active.name> ' at cursor position via slice(0,i) + insertText + slice(j). The state value (`draft`) at that moment already contains the '@' trigger that the user typed to open the menu. Nothing strips it. Backend regex `_MENTION_RE = r"@([A-Za-z]…)"` happens to be 'rescued' because it matches the inner @<Name>, so /api/messaging/conversations/{peer}/messages still returns mentions:[peer_id] and unread_count.mentions increments — verified end-to-end. Fix is local to insertMention(): walk back from el.selectionStart while previous char is not whitespace and not '@'; once you hit the latest '@' (or BOF), splice from that index instead of selectionStart. That single change makes the visual perfect and keeps the existing happy-path behavior when user clicks the menu without typing @ (cursor walk-back finds nothing → falls back to current behavior).
